Automated COLOR Sorting Conveyor

A smart conveyor that detects objects, reads their color with a TCS3200 sensor and sends each one to its own bin by itself.

How it works

  
One object at a time, from START to the final count.

  
    
    
  1. 1STARTThe START button runs the belt.
    2. 
    
  2. 2Entry IRAn infrared sensor sees the object and the belt stops.
    3. 
    
  3. 3TCS3200The sensor reads red, green and blue. A color is accepted after two identical readings.
    4. 
    
  4. 4Servo gateA servo gate moves to the bin of that color and the belt runs again.
    5. 
    
  5. 5Bin IRA sensor at the bin confirms the object. The counter goes up and is saved in memory.
    6. 
  

  
Red, green, blue and yellow go to their own bins. Anything else goes to the Unknown bin. The counts survive a power cut.






  
Objectives

  
    
    
  • Detect each object that arrives on the belt.
    • 
    
  • Identify its color with the TCS3200 sensor.
    • 
    
  • Divert it to the right bin with servo gates.
    • 
    
  • Count every object and keep the count after a power cut.
    • 
    
  • Show counters, last color, temperature and status on a 20x4 LCD.
    • 
    
  • Protect the user and the machine with START, STOP and EMERGENCY, a fault alarm and a temperature check.
    • 
  






  
Main components

  

    
ATmega32AMicrocontroller, 8 MHz, programmed in C.

    
TCS3200Color sensor with red, green, blue and clear filters.

    
TCRT5000 x6Infrared sensors at the entry and at each bin.

    
L293D + DC motorDrives the belt, speed set by PWM.

    
SG90 x2Servo gates, each one serving two bins.

    
LCD 20x4 (I2C)Counters, last color, temperature and status.

    
LM35Temperature sensor read by the on-chip ADC.

    
LM2596 + 12 V5 V supply for the logic from a 12 V adapter.

    
Lamps and buzzerGreen and red lamps and an alarm buzzer.

  






  
Safety

  

    
Normally closed buttonsSTOP and EMERGENCY are normally closed, so a broken wire counts as a press.

    
5 second watchdogIf an object does not reach its bin in 5 seconds, the machine stops with an alarm.

    
Emergency firstThe emergency button is checked first in every loop. At 35 °C or more for three readings, the machine stops too.

  






  
Build stages

  
From the first idea to the working machine.

  

    
Stage 1
Simulation
We tested the circuit logic in Proteus before building anything.

    
Stage 2
Breadboard
Eleven steps, and each one was tested before the next.

    
Stage 3
3D model
We designed the model in SolidWorks and fixed the place of each sensor, gate and bin.

    
Stage 4
PCB
The circuit moved to a printed board with labeled connectors.

    
Stage 5
Implementation
Everything assembled on the model, wired, tested and calibrated.
